title: Approaching the role of RcgA and RcgR
projectDescription: This study addresses the function of RcgA and RcgR, two proteins encoded near traR on pLPU83a, whose function has previously been associated with CT modulation. Through transcriptomic we show that RcgR functions as a repressor of CT, inhibiting traR expression and, as a consequence, the transcription of Dtr and Mpf genes
sampleProcessingProtocol: For cellular protein isolation, 1.5 mL of cell cultures were centrifugated at 13000 rpm for 5 minutes and pellets were frozen in N2. Pellets were resuspended in 100 µl of 100mM Ambic [ammonium bicarbonate (Honeywell Fluka)]. Next, 100 µl of the organic solvent trifluoroethanol (TFE, Fluka biochemika) and 5 µl of 20nM DTT were added. The tubes were mixed by inversion and incubated for 60 minutes at 60°C. In a second step, 20 μL of 200 mM Iodoacetamid (IAA) was added and placed for 90 min in the dark at room temperature. Then, 5 µl of 20nM DTT were added again and incubated for 60 minutes at room temperature. Half of the mixture was saved at -80 ºC as backup. To the remaining sample, 437 μL of 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate and 437 μL of bidistilled water were added. In the next step, 10 μL Trypsin Gold (1 μg μL−1) (Mass Spectrometry Grade, Promega, WI, USA) was added and the solution was incubated at 37 °C overnight.  The protein digestion was purified the next day with Sep Pak C18 cartridges (Waters Corporation, Milford, MA, USA). The Sep Pak C18 cartridges were rinsed with 1 mL of solution B (65% Acetonitril, 35% bidistilled water; 0.1% TFA). The column was equilibrated with 1 mL of solution A (98% Acetonitril, 2% bidistilled water; 0.1% TFA). Next, the digest mixed with 1 mL of solution A was added and run through the column slowly. Subsequently, the cartridges were washed with 1 mL of solution A. The proteome was eluted with 100 μL solution B in low protein binding collection tubes and dried in a vacufuge concentrator (Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany). Next, the dried peptide mixture was resuspended in 15 μL of solution A and quantified with a Nano-Drop™ 2000/2000c (Thermo Fisher, MA, USA).  LC-MS/MS measurements were carried out using a QExactive mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) online coupled to the LC system. The peptides were separated on a 25 cm steel column Acclaim™ PepMap™ 100 C18-LC-column with a particle size of 2 μm and a diameter of 75 μm (Thermo Fisher, MA, USA).  For extraction of extracellular proteins, 50 mL of cell cultures were centrifuged at 13000 rpm for 5 minutes and supernatants were filtered with 0,2 μm filters and frozen in N2. Then, the method developed by  Wendler et al. (2013) was followed. Briefly, the proteins of the freeze-dried supernatant were isolated by phenol extraction with subsequent methanol precipitation and several washing steps with 70% ethanol. After drying the extracellular proteins were resuspended in 200 μl TE-Buffer and 5 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) and incubated for 60 min at 60°C. 20 μL of 200 mM iodacetamid (IAA) was added and left for 90 min in the dark. Next, 5 μL of 200 mM DTT was added to the solution and incubated for additional 60 min. Extracellular proteins were digested following the same protocol as for the cellular fraction.
